summary: The retired boundHostFn implementation had no production call site; all of its invocations were standalone sandbox tests. The live async guest-to-host surface remains centralized in membrane.ts attachAsync, and the focused live-path suite proves the retained deadline, cancellation, result-cap, deferred teardown, async bridge, in-flight accounting, and bounded job-pump controls.

boundHostFnWasTestOnly.evidence: At 838a29e02^, git grep found the declaration/export plus calls only in tests/server/infra/plugin-host/sandbox.test.ts. No production caller existed.

boundHostFnFullyRetired.evidence: Current ast-grep finds zero boundHostFn calls in 5035 TS files and zero in 1406 TSX files; rg finds zero TS/TSX references. The function, imports, public re-export, standalone tests, and live-doc claims were removed.

attachAsyncSoleLiveWrapperAuthority.evidence: ast-grep finds 33 attachAsync nodes in TS: one local declaration and 32 construction calls, all in membrane.ts; zero TSX nodes. Sandbox creates every live membrane with a pending set and installs the CPU guard before installRealm. Synchronous capability and registration functions remain direct ctx.newFunction sites and do not create deferred promises.

properties.outboundResultCap: membrane.test.ts drives a normal storage.get result followed by HOST_FN_RESULT_CAP_BYTES+1 and proves the oversized value is rejected before crossing to guest
properties.deadlineAndCancellation: port.test.ts proves a host-function timeout aborts cooperative work and prevents its late side effect
properties.pendingTeardown: port.test.ts covers snippet/resident fire-and-forget teardown; escape.suite.test.ts covers the multi-pending drain and in-flight ceiling
properties.asyncBridge: membrane.test.ts and port.test.ts exercise real QuickJS deferred promise round trips through attachAsync
properties.boundedPumping: cpu-guard.test.ts proves pumpGuestJobs preempts runaway queued guest work; escape.suite.test.ts proves the live post-invocation attachAsync continuation is preempted and the slow-host control still completes
properties.inFlightAccounting: membrane.test.ts proves work outliving the deadline retains its slot; escape/port tests prove cross-invocation and teardown ownership

securityPropertyLost.evidence: The removed unregistered-context and standalone-wrapper tests covered the retired non-live primitive. guardOf remains fail-closed, every live Sandbox installs its guard, and the live escape/port/cpu suites retain the corresponding availability controls.

reachableExportLost.evidence: boundHostFn itself was a syntactically reachable @orb/server/infra/plugin-host export and was intentionally removed by the owner ruling. No other export changed, and no repository consumer imported it outside its standalone test. Therefore no unintended or live-consumed export was lost, but the literal claim that zero reachable export symbols were removed would be false.

structuralEvidence.rg: No boundHostFn TS/TSX references remain; attachAsync references are confined to the plugin-host membrane, Sandbox lifecycle comments, budget/cpu-guard law, and its proof corpus.
structuralEvidence.exportDiff: The only export-list removal is boundHostFn; EvalOutcome, GuestError, PLUGIN_INVOCATION_ENDED, Sandbox, SandboxLimits, budget constants, port, module, and realm exports remain.
